title: The Thick wall of the tower
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：thick　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 thick 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the musician wrote of ① a thick wall of the tower in the programme, and everybody in the hall said at once that it was ② thicker than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the musician, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the thick ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the thickest wall of the tower anybody in the hall had ever seen, or so the programme for December 1953 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too thick to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the thick ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a thick fog on the river, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as thick as the fog on the river they had once had in the old hall. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was thick or not, and he said so.

By 1966 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something thick, and nothing besides. The listener from the next hall called the whole plan ⑧ quite thick; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the thick ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1969, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another thick wall of the tower in the same programme, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ thicker than anybody had expected. ⑩ The thickest fog on the river in the whole hall, she said in 1971, was the one she could never quite name; the thick ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 厚（前置定语 a thick wall of the tower：1959 年乐师在节目单里记下的那件厚的墙）
B. adj. 厚／浓密（比较级 thicker than：文中两处，一处比塔的厚墙，一处比预想）
C. adj. 厚／浓密（最高级 the thickest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 厚（表语 too thick to do：母亲觉得它太厚，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 浓密（前置定语 a thick fog on the river：叔叔把整件事称作一桩浓密的浓雾）
F. adj. 浓密（同级比较 as thick as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩河上的浓雾相比）
G. adj. 浓密（后置定语 something thick：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 浓密（受程度副词修饰 quite thick：那位听客的评价）

items.q: a thick wall of the tower
the thickest wall of the tower anybody
a thick fog on the river
The thickest fog on the river in

answers.why: thick 意为“厚”，1959 年乐师在节目单里记下的是“一件厚的墙”，此处作前置定语 a thick wall of the tower。
thick 意为“厚”，此处用比较级 thicker than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
thick 意为“厚”，节目单上 十二月 那行字说它是音乐厅里最厚的一件，故用最高级 the thickest wall of the tower。
thick 意为“厚”，母亲认为这件东西“太厚了，谁也用不上”，too thick to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
thick 意为“浓密”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩浓密的浓雾”，此处作前置定语 a thick fog on the river。
thick 意为“浓密”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩河上的浓雾一样浓密”，同级比较用 as thick as。
thick 意为“浓密”，节目单上那半行字要的是“浓密的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something thick。
thick 意为“浓密”，邻音乐厅来的那位听客认为这套计划“相当浓密”，quite 修饰原级 thick。
thick 意为“浓密”，1969 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要浓密”，故用比较级 thicker than。
thick 意为“浓密”，母亲 1971 年说的是“整个音乐厅里最浓密的那一桩”，故用最高级 the thickest fog on the river。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1959 年，乐师在节目单里记下了一件厚的墙。（a thick wall of the tower）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更厚。（thicker than …）
母亲觉得它太厚，谁也用不上。（too thick to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩浓密的浓雾。（a thick fog on the river）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩河上的浓雾一样浓密。（as thick as …）
到了 1966 年，节目单上只剩半行字：要的是一件浓密的东西。（something thick）
answers: In 1959 the musician wrote of a thick wall of the tower in the programme.
Everybody said it was thicker than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too thick to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a thick fog on the river.
He said nobody would call it as thick as the fog on the river they had once had.
By 1966 the programme asked for nothing but something thick.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 thick 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the musician wrote of a thick wall of the tower in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the thickest wall of the tower in the hall, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too thick to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a thick fog on the river, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next hall called the plan quite thick, and everybody laughed.
The thick ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
